text: Let \(f(x) = \cos 2x + x\) on \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\). What is the least value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: Given \(f(x) = \cos 2x + x\) on \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\). Differentiate: \(f'(x) = -2\sin 2x + 1\). Set \(f'(x) = 0\), so \(\sin 2x = \frac{1}{2}\). On the interval, \(2x \in [-\pi, \pi]\), giving \(2x = \frac{\pi}{6}\) and \(2x = \frac{5\pi}{6}\), i.e. critical points \(x = \frac{\pi}{12}\) and \(x = \frac{5\pi}{12}\). Evaluate \(f\) at the critical points and the endpoints. At \(x = -\frac{\pi}{2}\): \(f = \cos(-\pi) - \frac{\pi}{2} = -1 - \frac{\pi}{2} = -\left(1 + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). At \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\): \(f = \cos\pi + \frac{\pi}{2} = -1 + \frac{\pi}{2}\). At \(x = \frac{\pi}{12}\): \(f = \cos\frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{\pi}{12} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{12}\) (about \(1.13\), the greatest). At \(x = \frac{5\pi}{12}\): \(f = \cos\frac{5\pi}{6} + \frac{5\pi}{12} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{5\pi}{12}\) (about \(0.44\)). The smallest of these is \(-\left(1 + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) at \(x = -\frac{\pi}{2}\). Hence the least value is \(-\left(1 + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), option A. Sibling Q85 (greatest value) is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{12}\), confirming the Direction is read correctly.
